title: Mid-configuration bounds after an update
statement: Let $A$ be a register program with $m$ registers, let $l_0,l$ be program states, let $v$ assign a natural number to each register, and let $out$ be a Boolean output word. Choose a register $r$, a state $s$ paired with a phase, an input-head position $ip$, and integers $q,W$. If the compiled program has no call at $s$, if $-1\le q\le W$, and if $0\le W$, then the configuration obtained by starting from the seam configuration for $l,v,out$ and setting its state to $s$, input-head position to $ip$, and register-head position at $r$ to $q$ is a mid-configuration: it has no call at its active state, and every register-head position lies between $-1$ and $W$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: The compiled program has no call at the specified state.
